messages:
inc-bot: INCIDENT created — OrionHealth (dedicated VPC pool) high error rate on function-calls (parser failures). Severity: P1. Alerts: 5xx >= 7% over 5m. Pager sent to oncall

ashley_oncall: I’m on it. Paging Miguel (runtime) and Sam (routing). Laura (CS) can you confirm if OrionHealth rolled anything out on their side?

laura_cs: pinged OrionHealth (account rep). they say they deployed a small change to their tool-adapter yesterday at 03:02 UTC but "should be backward-compatible". asking for trace IDs now.

miguel: grabbing logs from the dedicated pool. seeing lots of JSON parse errors at the adapter stage. sample error from logs: `jsonschema.ValidationError: Additional properties are not allowed ('details' was unexpected)`

miguel: sample payload that failed: ```
{"tool":"patient-search","args":{"query":"knee pain"},"result":{"status":"ok","items":[...],"details":{"source":"ehr-v2","confidence":0.92}}
```

miguel: the schema we validate against (parser v1) does NOT include `details` under `result`. looks like the tool adapter is returning an extra nested object. decoder fails and we drop the request -> 502 to customer.

sam_eng: thanks. two immediate mitigations: 1) add a tolerant parser shim to ignore unknown fields (fast), 2) route OrionHealth traffic to the previous, known-good model/adapter variant (safer). Which do we prefer for minimal blast radius?

ashley_oncall: preference: route to previous variant first (no code change on infra). do that as a hotfix while we prepare a shim for long-term. can we do a canary 10% -> 100%?

sam_eng: yes. updating routing policy now. command: ```
curl -X POST https://console.api/redwood/routing/update -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"tenant":"orionhealth","from_variant":"parser-v2","to_variant":"parser-v1","canary_percent":10}'
```

deploy-bot: routing update started (req id r-9a3f). applying canary 10% for OrionHealth to parser-v1.

ashley_oncall: monitoring metrics. miguel, can you also push a temporary tolerant JSON parser to the dedicated pool as rollback-safe shim? simple change to accept additional_properties: true in our validator lib.

miguel: I can push a hotfix: modify validator config and restart the adapter worker. steps: 
1) edit `/srv/adapter/schema/config.yaml` set `additionalProperties: true`
2) `systemctl restart adapter-worker` on pool nodes (rolling)

miguel: patch ready, but I want to run it on one node first. starting canary on node dp-04.

sre-bot: dp-04 restart completed. adapter health checks: OK. error rate on dp-04 dropped from 9.2% -> 0.8% in the last 60s. :thumbsup:

ashley_oncall: good. continuing ramp of routing canary to 50%. watching latency + error graphs. set alerts to page at > 2% 5xx.

laura_cs: OrionHealth replied — they did push a patch to their lambda that added `details` field. they apologize, will revert if needed but prefer we handle compat for now to avoid their rollback.

sam_eng: ramping canary to 50% now. deploy-bot status: ```
routing r-9a3f: 10% -> 50% -> in-progress````

miguel: pushing patch to all adapter workers (rolling) to enable tolerant parsing. command I used: ```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/adapter VALIDATOR_FLAGS=--allow-additional-properties=true
```

deploy-bot: adapter deployment rollout started (deployment/adapter) — rollout-id d-44c2. watch: `kubectl rollout status deployment/adapter -n inference`.

ashley_oncall: metrics after shard-level fixes: global error rate for OrionHealth dropped from 7.8% -> 1.1% across dedicated pool at canary 50%. latency unchanged. we can finish ramp to 100% if no regression in 10m.

miguel: note — tolerant parser masks schema drift; we need contract tests. adding task to follow-up.

laura_cs: OrionHealth wants to be informed before we flip back to their original adapter. they asked for a short post-change notification. I’ll draft.

ashley_oncall: agreed. final ramp to 100% in 5m unless objections.

sam_eng: doing final ramp. routing update complete. routing r-9a3f -> 100% parser-v1.

deploy-bot: routing update complete. d-44c2 rollout complete. adapter pods: 12/12 ready.

ashley_oncall: OrionHealth error rate now 0.3% over 5m. marking incident as mitigated for customer impact. we still have a residual error baseline from unrelated causes.

beth_ops: I’m taking the night handoff. pulling runbook for post-incident: - follow-up with OrionHealth (CS) - create regression test in eval harness for `result.details` field - add schema contract test in CI - prepare a small changelog for Dedicated docs about tolerant parsing behavior

ashley_oncall: ty. miguel and sam, please create tickets with steps + link to logs and the exact config diff. assign to eng-runtime and eng-platform.

miguel: tickets created: INF-4123 (shim + rollout), INF-4124 (schema contract tests), links added.

laura_cs: message to OrionHealth sent: "We've applied a temporary compatibility fix on Redwood's adapter to accept the new `details` field. Your team can keep the change; we'll follow up with a permanent contract test and a recommended adapter schema. — Laura (CS)"

ashley_oncall: closing the active pager. leaving incident channel open for postmortem notes. thanks everyone. :heart:

inc-bot: Incident P1 -> mitigated. Incident owner: ashley_oncall. Follow-up tasks: INF-4123, INF-4124. SLA impact: minor, no data exfiltration. Incident timeline saved at https://incidents.redwood/1789456789

beth_ops: will pick up tomorrow AM for a writeup. tagging @sre-bot to collect graphs for the postmortem.

sre-bot: collected graphs and pushed a summary to INF-4123.

ashley_oncall: handoff complete. Night oncall: beth_ops. Good job team!"
